findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema does not declare an index signature, validation will always fail
findings.body: The schema uses `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`, but those are computed property names that evaluate to the strings "ZodString" and "ZodOptional" at runtime, not TypeScript index signatures. As a result the parsed object must contain a literal `ZodString: number` property in addition to `access_token`, which OAuth token responses never have. Whenever the credential-sync flow is active, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` returns `{success: false}` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so every credential refresh attempted via the sync endpoint will fail.

findings.title: Returns SafeParseResult instead of parsed data; Google Calendar persists the wrapper
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `safeParse` result object (`{success: true, data: ...}`), but `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` consumes it as if it were the parsed key: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This causes the database row to be overwritten with `{success: true, data: {…token fields…}}` rather than the token fields themselves. On the next request `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail and the credential becomes effectively unusable.

findings.title: Mutates parsed result by setting refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token"
findings.body: If the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper does `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. The string "refresh_token" is not a valid OAuth refresh token; any caller that persists this object (directly or via spread) will end up storing a placeholder value, causing the next refresh attempt to fail with invalid_grant. This affects the standard schemas (e.g. `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, `googleCredentialSchema`) that mark `refresh_token` optional. The mutation also has no TypeScript escape hatch – the helper writes a property that may not exist on the inferred type.

findings.title: Sync endpoint returns a fetch Response while callers expect axios / typed token objects
findings.body:
When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. Several callers assume their original axios / jsforce shape:
- `hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`: treats the return value as `HubspotToken` and reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate` and `.expiresIn` (undefined on a Response) and writes back `expiryDate = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` → NaN persisted as the expiry.
- `zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`: read `tokenInfo.data.error`, `tokenInfo.data.expiryDate`, etc. on what is now a `Response` object – `undefined.error` throws.
- `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: reads `res?.data.access_token` – undefined, throwing on `.access_token`.
The sync path therefore crashes the refresh for several integrations instead of delegating to the user's endpoint.

findings.title: zoho-bigin passes credential.id where user.id is expected
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken(credentialId, credentialKey)` calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. `refreshOAuthTokens` then POSTs `calcomUserId=${credentialId}` (the `Credential.id`, not `User.id`) to the self-hoster's sync endpoint, so the parent cannot resolve the user. Every other caller (Hubspot, Office365 video, Lark, Webex, Zoom, ZohoCRM) correctly forwards `credential.userId`.

findings.title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time
findings.body: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` performs a non-constant-time string comparison, exposing the webhook secret to timing attacks. Anyone able to observe response latencies could recover the secret character by character. Because this single shared secret authorizes writes of OAuth credentials for arbitrary `userId` values (see below), a leaked secret enables full impersonation of any user via injected tokens. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers.

findings.title: Webhook allows writing OAuth tokens for any user with no per-user authorization
findings.body: The endpoint authenticates the caller only via the shared `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` header; the request body supplies `userId` directly. There is no binding between caller identity and the target user (no signature of the userId, no per-user secret, no replay protection/nonce, no rate limit). Anyone in possession of the secret can therefore upsert OAuth credentials for any userId, including admin accounts, and effectively impersonate them. Because the secret is also required to be 32 bytes for AES-256, a leak is catastrophic for the instance.

findings.title: findFirst + create/update upsert is racy
findings.body: The handler does a `findFirst` followed by separate `update`/`create` calls rather than a single `upsert`/transaction. Two concurrent webhook calls for the same `(userId, appSlug)` can both observe `appCredential === null` and both insert, leaving duplicate `Credential` rows for the same user/app and breaking the assumption made elsewhere in the codebase (larkcalendar, office365video, webex, zoom callbacks) that there is at most one credential per `(type, appId, userId)`.

findings.title: Unnecessary database round-trip before appStoreMetadata lookup
findings.body: The handler queries `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug } })` and then immediately re-resolves the same slug against the in-memory `appStoreMetadata` map. The DB call adds latency to a public webhook and is redundant: validating against `appStoreMetadata` directly (and 404ing if absent) gives the same behaviour without hitting Postgres.

findings.title: Header lookup uses env var verbatim, but Node lowercases request headers
findings.body: `req.headers` in Node stores header names in lowercase. The handler looks up `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. If an operator sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` to any mixed/upper-case value, the lookup is `undefined` and every request is rejected with 403, even when the secret itself is correct. The constant should be lowercased before use, or compared against `req.headers[name.toLowerCase()]`.

findings.title: Body validation throws and bubbles as 500 instead of returning 400
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a Zod error when the body is malformed. Next.js converts that into a generic 500, while the rest of the handler consistently returns structured 400/403/404 JSON. Callers (the self-hoster's parent app) will not be able to distinguish malformed payloads from server errors.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely
findings.body: `getClient` issues the refresh POST directly to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then runs it through `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, but it never routes through `refreshOAuthTokens`. The result is that for self-hosters that turn on `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, Salesforce refresh tokens continue to be exchanged against Salesforce directly instead of being fetched from the configured parent service – inconsistent with every other calendar/video integration modified here, and undermining the purpose of the feature for Salesforce users.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED combines two unrelated flags and yields a non-boolean
findings.body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. With an empty string for either env var this evaluates to the empty string (or the other env var), not `false`, and downstream code uses it as a truthy check (`if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)`) – empty string is falsy so it happens to work, but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` later does `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)`, so the semantics depend on whether the env var is the literal `"false"`/`"0"` or empty. Coerce to a boolean explicitly and either include `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` in the gate or document the partial activation mode.
